newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airport body switches 98 meeting to Sydney from HK.
newsitem.headline: Airport body switches 98 meeting to Sydney from HK.

text.p: Airports Council International (ACI), which groups the world's airports, has switched to Sydney its 1998 meeting that was due to held in Hong Kong, an ACI spokesman said.

Hong Kong's decision to withdraw was related to the burden of work associated with opening of the territory's new airport at Chep Lap Kok (CLK in April next year and no other reasons were involved, he said.
Sydney was chosen as ACI wanted to hold its eighth annual meeting in the Asia-Pacific area despite Hong Kong's decision, he added. It will take place between November 1-4, 1998.
"We're still hopeful of holding a meeting in Hong Kong, but it will be after 2001 as we have Geneva in 1999, Montreal in 2000 and Santiago in 2001, " the spokesman said.
Beijing airport joined ACI in late 1996 while Shanghai, Guangzhou and Xiamen airports have told ACI officials that they intend to join the organisaton in the near future.

The deputy director of the Civil Aviation Administration of China(CAAC), Wang Ronghua, told ACI secretary-general Alexander Strahl in April that the CAAC would recommend that all of China's international airports eventually join ACI.
The organisation, which is holding its current annual meeting in Paris, has 475 members representing 1,200 airports in 150 countries.
